title: Fastpath interrupt coalescence scratch
summary: Quick scratchpad for a small experiment exploring how interrupt coalescence windows on the fastpath scheduler affect end-to-end tail latency under bursty ingress. Goal: validate whether increasing coalescence (micro-batching at interrupt level) reduces GPU kernel churn without inflating p99 beyond SLA.
experiment_notes: Context: recent customer reported p99 spikes during 200-400 qps short bursts. Hypothesis: frequent preempt/resume cycles on fastpath (small-kv cache warmups) cause kernel thrashing. Idea: introduce a short interrupt coalescence window (2-10ms) to let tiny bursts coalesce on CPU before handing off to GPU. Setup: single-node dedicated backend (A10x1 testfleet), model: llama-7b-int8 (serving-optimized build), runtime: v0.18.3-rc. Test harness: custom loadgen (poisson arrivals, bursty sessions), instrumented with trace-id passthrough to correlate kernel launches with request spans. Logged kernel timestamps + NVTX and runtime scheduler events. NOTE: this is a scratchpad — rough, noisy runs, not yet statistically rigorous.
raw_results: Run A (baseline, coalesce=0ms): avg_qps=305, p50=34ms, p90=82ms, p95=130ms, p99=460ms, errors=0.6% (timeouts)
Run B (coalesce=2ms): avg_qps=298, p50=36ms, p90=78ms, p95=120ms, p99=210ms, errors=0.2%
Run C (coalesce=5ms): avg_qps=290, p50=39ms, p90=82ms, p95=128ms, p99=170ms, errors=0.1%
Run D (coalesce=10ms): avg_qps=272, p50=45ms, p90=98ms, p95=180ms, p99=320ms, errors=0.4%

Micro-observation: kernel_launch_count per second dropped ~27% going from 0ms->5ms; average kernel duration increased slightly (hot kernel amortization) but reduction in context switches observed in scheduler traces.

Per-request trace snippet (baseline): many requests show GPU kernel restart within same trace due to preempt; with coalesce=5ms, traces show single contiguous kernel execution for batches of 2-5 tiny requests.

Error breakdown: most timeouts were tail spikes (>1s) correlating to cold-kv cache misses + preempted kernels when bursts overlap with autoscaler scaling events. Coalescence reduces overlap frequency.

Notes on throughput: measurable reduction in sustained qps at larger coalescence windows (>=10ms) because artificial delay queues incoming requests; tradeoff space exists (2-5ms sweet spot for this workload).
quick_conclusions: Short coalescence windows (2-5ms) materially reduce p99 (roughly 50% reduction vs baseline) while keeping p50/p90 nearly unchanged — good win for bursty tiny-request workloads.
Too-large windows (>=10ms) harm p50 and throughput; user-visible latency increases and qps drops — avoid for latency-sensitive routes.
Mechanism: fewer kernel launches + better kernel amortization > reduced scheduler churn => fewer long-tail preemptions.
Open risk: interactions with autoscaler and dedicated burst capacity need testing; coalescence may hide load signals and delay scaling reactions.
This should be an opt-in per-route policy (fastpath coalescence) with tunable ms and safe upper bound default (5ms).
